# backup: allow a bundle `out` under `source` when it lies outside every selected item

Source: hold stub 00117, promoted 2026-11-02 from the deferred finding of batch `202610292344` (ledger `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred/202610292344-deferred.json`, HIGH, raised against 00109 cycle 1). Depends on nothing open: 00109 and 00110 are done.

## Overview

### Problem Statement
`_reject_out_inside_source` in `src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py` refuses any `out` whose resolved path equals or lies under the resolved `source`. Both `TarArchive.run` and `_plan_source` call it before `items` is considered. The guard exists so a whole-tree archive never re-archives its own previous output. A bundle archives only its selected items, so the 00109 headline case is refused although the archive can never contain itself:

```yaml
instances:
  settings:
    use: tar-archive
    with:
      source: "~"
      items: [.gitconfig, .npmrc]
      out: ~/.local/backup/settings.tar.gz
```

Today this fails with `out path ... is inside source ...` for `backup`, `backup --dry-run` and `backup --plan`.

### Target Users
The solo operator who keeps a bundle of home-directory config files and wants the archive under the same home directory.

### Success Metrics
- `uv run pytest tests/tools/backup/test_bundle_items.py tests/tools/backup/test_plan_validation.py -q` passes with the new cases.
- The whole-tree containment tests in `tests/tools/backup/test_tar_archive.py` (`test_out_inside_source_fails_no_archive`, `test_stamped_out_inside_source_fails`) pass unchanged.

## Functional Decomposition

### Capability: Bundle output containment
Decide whether `out` can be written for the archive that will actually be produced.

#### Feature: Item-scoped containment
- **Description**: With `items` set, containment is checked against the selected items instead of `source`.
- **Inputs**: resolved `source`, `out` (parent resolved, name rejoined, as today), the normalized selected items from `_normalize_items`.
- **Outputs**: unchanged `StepResult` / plan row contract.
- **Behavior**:
  - `items` omitted or `null`: unchanged. `out` equal to or under `source` fails with the existing message.
  - `items` set: `out` equal to `source` still fails with the existing message. `out` equal to or under `source / item` for any selected item fails with `out path {out} is inside selected item {source/item}; choose an out path outside the bundle's items`. Any other `out` is allowed, including one under `source`.
  - Items are validated first: an invalid `items` value keeps its existing message and wins over containment, because containment needs the normalized items.
  - `run`, `--dry-run` and `--plan` agree: the plan row is `fail` with the same reason the run would yield, and `run` for the allowed case is `run`.
  - A later run of the allowed case, when `out` already exists under `source`, still succeeds and the previous archive is not a member (it lies outside every item).

## Structural Decomposition

### Repository Structure

```
src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py          # Maps to: Item-scoped containment
tests/tools/backup/test_bundle_items.py               # Maps to: run and dry-run cases
tests/tools/backup/test_plan_validation.py            # Maps to: plan cases
docs/source/tools/backup.rst                          # Maps to: documentation
CHANGELOG.md                                          # Maps to: documentation
```

### Module: tar_archive
- **Maps to capability**: Bundle output containment
- **Responsibility**: pick the containment roots (source, or the selected items) and reject `out` inside any of them.
- **Location**: `src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py`
- **Exports**: none new; `_reject_out_inside_source` gains the item-scoped branch (or a sibling helper), and both `run` and `_plan_source` normalize items before calling it.

## Dependency Graph

### Foundation Layer (Phase 0)
- **tar_archive**: no dependencies.

### Integration Layer (Phase 1)
- **docs**: depends on [tar_archive].

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 0: Core
**Goal**: The headline bundle case runs, plans and dry-runs; outputs inside a selected item are still refused.

**Tasks**:
- [ ] Add the item-scoped containment branch in `src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py` and call it from `run` and `_plan_source` after items are normalized (no deps) - Acceptance: `uv run pytest tests/tools/backup/test_bundle_items.py tests/tools/backup/test_plan_validation.py tests/tools/backup/test_tar_archive.py -q` passes, parametrized over `python-tarfile` and `system-tar` where the file already does so.

**Exit Criteria**: source with `.gitconfig` and `.npmrc`, `items: [.gitconfig, .npmrc]`, `out: <source>/.local/backup/settings.tar.gz` archives exactly the two members in both engines; `items: [.config]` with `out: <source>/.config/x.tar.gz` fails without writing.

### Phase 1: Integration
**Goal**: Documented.

**Tasks**:
- [ ] Add one sentence to the "Selected items" section of `docs/source/tools/backup.rst` stating that a bundle's `out` may lie under `source` but not inside a selected item; add a `Fixed` line under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` prefixed `**backup**:` (depends on: Phase 0) - Acceptance: `rg -c "selected item" docs/source/tools/backup.rst` prints at least 1 and `rg -c "selected item" CHANGELOG.md` prints at least 1.

**Exit Criteria**: `uv run pytest tests/tools/backup -q` passes; `uv run ruff check src/tools/backup tests/tools/backup` and `uv run mypy src/tools/backup` are clean.

## Test Strategy

### Critical Scenarios
- **Happy path**: `items: [.gitconfig, .npmrc]`, `out` under `<source>/.local/backup/` → Expected: success, members exactly `.gitconfig` and `.npmrc`, both engines.
- **Happy path, second run**: same config with the archive already present → Expected: success, archive replaced, the archive is not a member.
- **Edge case**: `items: [.config]`, `out: <source>/.config/x.tar.gz` → Expected: failed step naming the selected item, no file written, existing `out` bytes unchanged.
- **Edge case**: `items: [.config]`, `out` equal to `<source>/.config` → Expected: failed step (equality counts as inside).
- **Edge case**: `items` omitted, `out` under `source` → Expected: existing failure and message (unchanged tests).
- **Plan**: `--plan` rows for the happy path and the inside-item case are `run` and `fail` with the run's reason.
- **Error case**: `items: []` with `out` under `source` → Expected: the existing `items must not be empty` message, not a containment message.

## Risks

- **Symlinked items**: an item that is a symlink to a directory holding `out` is archived as a link, never followed, so `out` is not re-archived. No extra check.
- **Stamped outputs**: `out` with `strftime` codes resolves its parent as today; a stamped basename under a selected directory is still rejected because the parent is inside the item.

Reviewers get isolated contexts by construction (subagent prompts, external CLIs); the review phase itself runs in a fresh session after the build hand-off (end the turn: set `state.next_phase`, print the banner, STOP; in loop mode the headless session exits and the `autoclaude` wrapper relaunches from `state.json`). Never invoke `/autopilot:review-work-completion` from the work session, even if context budget appears sufficient. Scope (decided 2026-09-14, discovery 00203): this rule governs the full lane and every fast-track roster. Lane routing is decided by code (`cli/lane.py`, autopilot PRD 00204), never by an agent's judgment; the solo lane's one-pass zero-context review of docs/test-only PRDs, with code-decided escalation to the full gate on any production or security-ish diff, a CRITICAL or a surviving HIGH (PRD 00205), is the user's design, not an agent thinning the review.
- After completing work, clean up stale worktrees, orphan branches, temp files, and executed plan files in the repo's `docs/dev/project-management/plans/`.
- Meta-budget: Claude-on-Claude work (the `~/.claude` project) targets <= 30% of monthly spend; the portfolio brief surfaces the share monthly (red above ceiling). Released-plugin repo work counts as product, not meta.
- If a secret may have been exposed, rotate it.

## Compaction

- After failed approach: compact
- Mid-implementation: don't compact
- After completing a PRD, before next: compact

With 1M context, research stays in-flight through implementation.

## Planning

- End plans with unresolved questions.
- One question at a time, concise, with enough context to answer quickly.

## Handing work to the user

The user runs a hand-off top to bottom and does not read ahead. Write it so that order is safe.

- One numbered list, steps in execution order, commands inline. A precondition is its own step placed before the step that needs it. A warning that applies to a step comes before that step, never after the list. Mark an optional step optional in its place. Put nothing after the list that changes how to run it. (2026-10-17, PRD 00163: the approve commands came first and the config fix came below them, so the commit went out without the fix.)
- Write hand-offs in Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100): one instruction per sentence, imperative mood, present tense, at most 20 words, one word for one meaning, no idioms, no synonyms for the same thing. State the expected result of a step when the user needs it to continue.

- Interactive agent sessions start via `~/bin/run-agent`, which runs the agent under the macOS Seatbelt profile `~/.config/seatbelt/ai-agents.sb`: reads of `~/.config/gh`, private keys and similar are denied, writes land only under the project, `~/git/src`, `~/.claude`, `~/.cache`, `~/Library/Caches`, `~/Library/Logs`, `~/.local/state`, agent state dirs, data-only package caches and temp dirs. No tool bin dir or install target is writable (`~/.local/share/mise`, `~/.config/mise`, `~/Applications`, `~/.local/share/claude` and `~/.local/bin` are read-only since 2026-10-17): install or update tools through warrant, e.g. `~/bin/warrant request --reason "..." -- mise install <tool>`. The Keychain is reachable for Claude Code's own item (verified 2026-10-29); other `security` secret reads have failed with exit 36. Since 2026-10-29 the launcher exports `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `~/.local/secret/claude-setup-token`, so sessions never refresh the shared Keychain OAuth login (concurrent refreshes revoked it about twice a day, anthropics/claude-code#24317); on the setup-token `/login`, `/usage` and the claude.ai MCP connectors (Docs, Context7, Reader) are unavailable, and `RUN_AGENT_CLAUDE_LOGIN=1 run-agent claude` opts one session back into the Keychain login. - An operation the profile denies (for example a commit in the bare `~/.buvis` repo) goes through **warrant** (PRD 00159): run `~/bin/warrant request --reason "..." -- CMD ARG...` from the sandbox, with `--no-wait` or in the background because the request may wait hours, then `~/bin/warrant wait ID`. The user reviews and runs it outside the sandbox with `~/bin/warrant approve` and a PIN. Never try to approve, read `~/.config/warrant`, or work around a refusal.
- CLI tools and language runtimes are managed with **mise**. Installs live under `~/.local/share/mise/installs/<tool>/<version>/`; shims at `~/.local/share/mise/shims/`.
- Global `npm ls -g`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` will NOT list mise-managed tools - don't conclude a tool is missing from those. Locate one with `mise which <tool>`; run one not on PATH via `mise exec -- <tool>`.

- Not every install gets a shim - `mise which` can resolve a tool even when `command -v` fails. If a tool is missing from PATH, run `mise reshim` through warrant (the shims dir is read-only in the sandbox).
- The default model carries `[1m]` (1M window). The autopilot context cap (`autopilot_context_cap_hook.USAGE_CAP` in the autopilot plugin's `skills/run-autopilot/scripts/`, mirrored in `tracon/model.py` beside it) is 500K, coupled to that 1M default: never drop it toward 150K unless the default window also shrinks below 200K, or the cap misfires at ~163K aborting healthy build sessions (PRD 00073; 150K pin reverted 2026-07-20 when `[1m]` was restored).

## Dotfiles repo

- Tracked in a bare repo at `~/.buvis`, work-tree is `$HOME`. Run git as `git --git-dir=~/.buvis --work-tree=~ <cmd>` (no shell alias assumed).
- **This repo answers "not tracked" by staying silent. That has already caused a wrong conclusion.** Treat ANY empty output from `~/.buvis` as unverified until a known-tracked control path proves the command shape works.
  - The index IS populated and matches HEAD (verified 2026-08-17: `ls-files` and `ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD` both return 641 entries), so `ls-files` is a valid tracking check. Still prefer `git diff HEAD` over plain `git diff`: the index is shared with the user's live sessions, so anything they staged is invisible to an index-vs-worktree diff.
  - Pathspecs resolve against **cwd**, not the work-tree. From anywhere but `~`, `-- .claude/foo` silently searches `<cwd>/.claude/foo` and finds nothing. Anchor every pathspec with `:(top)`, e.g. `add ':(top).claude/rules/foo.md'`. `git log` and `show --stat` keep working regardless, which makes the repo look fine while the path looks absent.
- The `rules/changelog.md` mandate does **not** apply here: no releases, no CHANGELOG. Commit `feat`/`fix` directly without a CHANGELOG entry, and don't add a CHANGELOG.md to this repo.
# AGENTS.md

BUVIS gems monorepo. Python toolkit (buvis-pybase + zettel) and CLI tools, shipped as a single PyPI package `buvis-gems`. Supports Python 3.11+.

## Reading these instructions

This root `AGENTS.md` is the always-on canonical guidance. Some directories also
carry their own nested `AGENTS.md` with rules scoped to the code beside them.
Before working on files in a directory, discover and read any `AGENTS.md` on the
path from the repo root down to that directory, and follow it for files in its
scope. Do this yourself even if your host did not load those files automatically
— host loading of nested files varies and is not guaranteed (see
[`docs/dev/architecture/agent-host-support.md`](docs/dev/architecture/agent-host-support.md)).

## Quick Start


```text
src/

│   ├── adapters/               # jira, console, config adapters

│   ├── formatting/             # output formatting

│       ├── domain/             # entities, services, interfaces, value objects
│       ├── application/        # use cases
│       ├── infrastructure/     # formatters, repositories, file parsers
│       └── integrations/       # jira assemblers
└── tools/
    ├── bim/                    # BUVIS InfoMesh CLI (zettel integration)
    ├── dot/                    # dotfiles manager
    ├── fctracker/              # foreign currency tracker
    ├── fren/                   # file renamer toolkit
    ├── morph/                  # file conversion toolkit

    ├── netscan/                # network scanning tools

tests/
├── lib/                        # library tests
│   ├── pybase/
│   ├── zettel/
│   └── zettel_integrations/
└── tools/                      # CLI tool tests
tools/                          # Dev command shims (on PATH via mise) + helpers

```

**Key patterns:**

- **Single package**: `buvis-gems` on PyPI, one `uv tool install`
- **Namespace package**: `src/lib/buvis/` has no `__init__.py`
- **Hatch packages**: each `src/tools/<name>/` maps to top-level `<name>` in wheel
- **Libraries are internal**: pybase + zettel not published separately
- **All-interface rule**: every command/action must work across CLI, TUI, API, and WebUI

## Tool Structure

Every tool under `src/tools/<name>/` follows a base layout:

```text
tool_name/
├── __init__.py
├── __main__.py
├── cli.py              # Click entry point
├── settings.py         # Tool-specific settings
└── commands/           # One module per CLI command
```

Add subdirs only when needed:

| Dir | When | Example |
|-----|------|---------|
| `adapters/` | External service clients | fctracker, readerctl |
| `domain/` | Business logic beyond simple commands | fctracker |
| `shared/` | Code reused across commands | zseq |

> `bim/commands/serve/frontend/` contains the WebUI SvelteKit app — the only tool with a frontend subtree.

> `bim/commands/doc/` follows the existing `commands/serve/`-style group pattern with a `shared/` subdir holding cross-command utilities (pipeline, OCR/classifier/extractor adapters, state DB, issuer registry, zettel writer).

## Code Conventions

**Type hints** — modern style, no `Optional`:

```python
from __future__ import annotations
def foo(path: Path | None = None) -> list[str]: ...
```

**Imports**:

- Explicit `__all__` in `__init__.py`
- `TYPE_CHECKING` guards for type-only imports

**Docstrings**: Google format

**CLI pattern**: Click-based. `buvis_options` adds `--version`, `--config`, `--log-level`, `--debug`, and `--update` to every tool automatically:

```python
@click.command()
@buvis_options
@click.pass_context
def cli(ctx: click.Context) -> None:
    settings = get_settings(ctx)
    ...
```

**Lazy imports in CLI handlers**: import command classes inside handler functions, not at module level. This avoids pulling in optional/heavy dependencies before the user picks a subcommand:

```python
@cli.command("create")
@click.pass_context
def create(ctx):
    from bim.commands.create_note.create_note import CommandCreateNote
    ...
```

## Error Handling

**Command layer** (`commands/`):
- Return `CommandResult` for all outcomes — success and failure
- Catch expected exceptions (e.g. `FileNotFoundError`) internally, return `CommandResult(success=False, error=str(exc))`
- No `console.panic()` or `sys.exit()` inside command classes
- No custom exception classes for control flow

**CLI layer** (`cli.py`):
- Inspect `CommandResult` and call `console.panic()` / `console.failure()` / `console.success()`
- Use `console.report_result()` for standardized output
- Catch `ImportError` for optional deps, call `console.require_import()`
- Catch `FatalError` for unrecoverable infrastructure failures

**Click argument validation**:
- Avoid parse-time validators that short-circuit before the callback (`click.Path(exists=True)`, `IntRange`, custom `ParamType.convert` that raises). They emit Click's default `Usage: ... Error: ...` formatting and bypass the buvis console.
- Validate inside the callback instead: `if not path.is_file(): console.panic(f"file not found: {path}"); return`.
- `click.Choice` is the exception — its parse-time error lists the valid values, which is more useful than a rewritten message.

**Console methods**:
- Fatal (exit): `console.panic(msg)` — prints + exits with code 1
- Recoverable: `console.failure(msg)` — prints, continues
- Status: `console.success()`, `console.warning()`, `console.info()`
- All user-facing output must route through `console`. No `print()`, `sys.stdout.write()`, `sys.stderr.write()`, `click.echo()`, `click.secho()`, or the Python logging module. Plain writes bypass the buvis prefix markers (`✘`, `✓`, etc.) and become indistinguishable from stray output, which is what makes a missed `console.panic` look like a print statement to the user.
- The one sanctioned exception is the `dot filter` clean/smudge plumbing, which writes git's blob payload as raw bytes on stdout and at most one error line on stderr, because git owns both streams and a console marker would corrupt the payload (discovery R12).
- Never let raw exceptions (stack traces) reach the user.

## Invariants (evolution guardrails)

These encode the failure classes surfaced by the 2026-07-09 evolution assessment (`docs/dev/project-management/reviews/evolution-assessment-2026-07-09.md`). Each is either **HOLDS** (enforce it) or a **GAP** (a tracked PRD is closing it — write new code to the target state, not the current one).

- **Atomic persistence** — never persist a note, state file, or config with a bare `Path.write_text`/`open(...,"w")`. Use `pybase.filesystem.atomic_write` (tempfile + fsync + `os.replace`). Truncate-then-write loses data on crash/ENOSPC. *HOLDS for the library and note/updater write paths (00041) — keep it, except `ConfigWriter.write` (`configuration/config_writer.py`), which still does a bare `write_text` — deliberately out of scope for 00041. GAP → pidash was closed by retiring pidash (00071); autopilot-state durability now lives in the buvis home repo (tracon/statectl), not gems.*
- **Confine request-derived paths** — any filesystem path built from an HTTP request / external input must be `resolve()`d and asserted under an allowed root before read/write/delete/open. Network-facing servers must have auth + `TrustedHostMiddleware`. *HOLDS (00042) — bim serve confines request paths via `confine_path` (403 outside the vault/archive roots), mints a startup token required as `X-Buvis-Token`, installs `TrustedHostMiddleware`, and warns on a non-loopback bind (`commands/serve/_security.py`). Keep it.*
- **The library stays interface-agnostic** — `src/lib/buvis/pybase/` must not import a UI framework at module import time or emit output outside the console adapter. No import-time Click monkey-patching, no `sys.exit`/`click.echo`/`print` in lib code. A TUI/API/WebUI process must be able to `import` settings without pulling Click. *HOLDS (00052) — keep it.*
- **One action, one implementation across interfaces** — CLI/TUI/API/WebUI adapters must drive the same command class / use case through the composition root and return `CommandResult`; do not reimplement business logic per interface (dot's TUI is the anti-pattern; bim's serve action registry is the exemplar). *HOLDS (00051 design → 00053/00054) — the all-interface seam design (00051) is realized: dot's git ops unified behind `DotGitService` (00053) and bim's serve/TUI converged on the shared action registry (00054). Keep it.*
- **Claim/lifecycle release on any exit** — resource claims and locks release in `finally` (or catch `BaseException`), never only `except Exception`; `KeyboardInterrupt` must not leak a claim. *HOLDS (00044) — the bim doc claim/dedup pipeline releases claims and locks in `finally` (`commands/doc/shared/`); keep it.*
- **`CommandResult` discipline** — commands return `CommandResult`; the CLI/adapter layer renders it (`console.report_result`) and maps exit/HTTP status. No `sys.exit`/`console.panic` inside command classes. *HOLDS in `src/tools/*/commands/**` — keep it.*
- **Clean-architecture layering + tool isolation** — zettel `domain → application → infrastructure → integrations` one-directional; no cross-tool imports; no `src/lib → src/tools`. *HOLDS — keep it.*

## Testing

- pytest + pytest-mock + pytest-cov
- Tests in `tests/` mirror `src/lib/` and `src/tools/` structure
- Mock subprocess calls heavily
- Class-based test organization
- **No unused imports/variables**
- **Markers**: `pytest -m <tool>` runs one tool, `pytest -m lib` runs library tests, `pytest -m "not bim"` excludes a tool. Auto-applied by path in `tests/conftest.py` — no decorators needed. Scaffold registers markers for new tools.
- **Snapshot tests** (`@pytest.mark.snapshot`) only run on the canonical env (Linux + Python 3.12) — SVG output from Rich/Textual differs across OS/Python so baselines must come from one place. Anywhere else they are auto-skipped. To regenerate baselines run the `update-snapshots` GitHub workflow (`gh workflow run update-snapshots.yml`); it runs `pytest --snapshot-update` on the canonical env and commits the result. Force locally with `BUVIS_SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL=1` only if you know what you're doing.

> Full procedure (version authority, checks, destinations, partial-failure recovery): `docs/dev/procedures/releasing.md`.


**First-time setup** (already done for buvis-gems):
- test.pypi.org: add trusted publisher (owner: `buvis`, repo: `gems`, workflow: `publish.yml`, env: `testpypi`)
- GitHub repo settings: create `testpypi` and `pypi` environments

**Why explicit version in pyproject.toml?** maturin reads the version from `pyproject.toml` at build time to compile the Rust extension. Tag-based versioning (hatch-vcs) would require glue to inject the version before maturin sees it. Pure Python projects like mkdocs-zettelkasten use hatch-vcs instead — the version derives from the git tag, no file to keep in sync, no bump commits.

# Autopilot

Orchestrate the full PRD lifecycle: catchup → design → plan-tasks → work → review-rework loop (consensus + blind + doubt lenses, every cycle) → done.

Makes autonomous decisions backed by research (dependencies, recurring issues, API/schema changes when PRD-driven) and pauses only for critical security, requirements ambiguity, or blocking decisions.

## Dependencies

- Pack skills (invoked as phases): `design-solution`, `plan-tasks`, `work`,
  `review-work-completion`
- Plugin skills: `git-ferry:catchup` (Phase 1, unless the PRD sets `catchup: skip`)
- Files read from other skill dirs:
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py`
  (Watcher keep-alive)
- Hooks outside the skill dir: `~/.claude/hooks/notify.py`
- Shell wrapper outside `~/.claude`: `autoclaude` in
  `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash` - operator subcommands +
  tracon front-end; it hands off to `autopilot loop` (`cli/loop.py`), the
  unattended session loop since PRD 00106
- Scripts (own dir, model-invoked as a CLI): `scripts/statectl.py` — the sole
  `state.json` mutator (`get`/`set`/`append`/`del`; atomic, advisory-locked,
  one rotating `.bak`)
- CLIs: `claude` (headless `-p`), `python3` (>= 3.11), `git`, `awk`
- Optional: `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`; the default `autoclaude` front-end since PRD 00062, `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0` or no tty/`uv` falls back to `render_stream.py`) - dashboard only, absence changes nothing

## Execution Model

**Run all phases in sequence without stopping.** After each phase completes, immediately update state and proceed to the next phase. Do not pause between phases, do not summarize progress, do not wait for user input - unless the phase explicitly says PAUSE or STOP. Completing a sub-skill invocation (`/git-ferry:catchup`, `/autopilot:plan-tasks`, `/autopilot:work`, `/autopilot:review-work-completion`, etc.) is NOT a stopping point. It is an intermediate step. Continue.

Review sessions run on opus at xhigh in cycle 1 and at high on cycle 2 and later; _AUTOPILOT_EFFORT_REVIEW forces one effort for every cycle and _AUTOPILOT_EFFORT_REVIEW_RERUN sets the rerun value. A rework resume (the cycle's review file exists and `rework_task_ids` names an unfinished task) runs on the queued tasks' own tier instead, sonnet unless one is opus or fable (`references/model-ladder.md` § Review sessions, PRD 00207).

## Entry Points

- `/autopilot:run-autopilot` — auto-select PRD (wip first, then backlog), run full cycle
- `/autopilot:run-autopilot <prd-filename>` — full cycle with specific PRD
- `/autopilot:run-autopilot status` — print current dashboard, no action
- `/autopilot:run-autopilot review-batch` — interactively review a finished batch's deferred items

If invoked with `status`, read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json`, print phase/cycle/task summary, and stop.

If invoked with `review-batch`, load the newest `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred/{batch_id}-deferred.json` and run the "Batch-End Review" presentation (`references/phase-done.md`) against it — chunked by PRD, wait for user decisions, execute "fix now" items. No state changes; the batch is already closed. Stop when all chunks are reviewed (or the user says stop).

Preflight for a batch rooted at `~/.claude`: the launching shell must `export _AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE_EXTRA="$HOME/.config/bash:$HOME/.codex:$HOME/.local/bin"`, or the write-scope fence (`hooks/enforce_write_scope.py`) false-denies edits under those roots and the task parks; `_AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE=off` disarms the fence for the batch.

## Gate Dispatch

The full per-phase instructions live in three gate reference files; this core deliberately carries only the shared contract plus the invariants below. After the entry-point checks, read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` and **Read the matching gate file now; do not execute a gate from memory**:

A state carrying `stall_op` runs `autopilot park` to reconcile before any gate file is read.

| resume state | Read this gate file |
|--------------|---------------------|
| `phase: "build"` — or `state.json` missing (fresh start) | `references/phase-build.md` |
| `phase: "review"` — or a legacy `"blind"`/`"doubt"` value (pre-00015 state), which maps to `review` | `references/phase-review.md` |
| `phase: "done"` | `references/phase-done.md` |
| `phase: "paused"` — or `stall_reason` set | `references/phase-build.md` (its Phase 0 abort/pause handlers own this resume) |

`status` and `review-batch` invocations do not dispatch a gate (see Entry Points).

## State Management

All autopilot artifacts live under `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/`, organized by type:

```
docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/
  state.json                              # current cycle state
  last-session.log                        # loop-teed raw output of the last headless session
  reports/{batch_id}-report.md            # batch audit report
  deferred/{batch_id}-deferred.json       # unresolved items across PRDs
```

State file: `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — see `references/state-schema.md` for schema.

**`statectl` is the sole writer of `state.json`.** Apply every field mutation with `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set|append|del <json-path> <json-value>` (read one field with `get`); it takes an advisory lock, backs up to `<state.json>.bak`, changes only the named path while preserving all siblings, and replaces the file atomically — so it cannot leave a half-written or unparseable state, and it never trips the "not read yet" / "modified since read" errors the editing tools hit. Since PRD 00089 it is a shim over `cli/state.transaction`, so every write is schema-validated too: a value that is malformed **for the field it targets** is rejected with exit 1 and the file left byte-unchanged (an unrelated pre-existing odd field blocks nothing). **Phase transitions are not field mutations** — use `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` (§ Session handoff procedure), never a hand-written `set phase` / `set next_phase` pair, so a transition cannot land without the effects it mandates. Resolve `<state.json>` by walking up from the resolved physical cwd to the autopilot dir (the `_walk_up.py` pattern in `/autopilot:work` step 2). The terse `set X` / `write field Y` / per-PRD-reset instructions throughout these skills and the gate files name the fields to change; each is applied with `statectl`, never by hand-editing the file.

Documented human fallback: outside the loop a person may still Edit or Write `state.json` by hand (for forensics or recovery — the model itself never hand-edits `state.json`; a statectl failure has its own marker-based recovery below); `validate_state_json_hook.py` catches a hand-edit that leaves the file unparseable and now also runs `cli.schema.validate` on it, and `statectl` reads whatever valid JSON it finds on its next mutation.

**When `statectl` itself fails** (nonzero exit — advisory-lock contention, a Python error, an unreadable `state.json`): retry the exact command ONCE. If it fails again, do NOT improvise a partial write and do NOT proceed on the stale state — a lost mutation strands the loop on the wrong `next_phase`. Run `autopilot restore` (rolls `state.json` back to `<state.json>.bak`) and retry the statectl command once more. If the failure persists (`autopilot restore` itself fails, or the subsequent statectl write still fails), WRITE THE MARKER `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state-write-failed` with the Write tool — ONE line of JSON `{"site": "statectl_fail", "detail": "<the statectl command and its raw stderr>"}` — and END THE TURN: the wrapper halts on the marker and surfaces the `detail` itself, so no further state write is needed. Interactive sessions ALSO report the same failure to the user directly (there is no wrapper watching an interactive terminal). The raw stderr rides into the marker's `detail` so the failure is diagnosable, never silent (`rules/operating-principles.md`). (Lock contention on the single-writer model implies a second loop or a stale lock; the concurrent-loop guard below now refuses a second loop up front, so a persistent lock is a stale one — the retry clears it or the marker records it.)

Create `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/` and subdirectories if missing. Initialize state file at PRD selection. Update state at every phase transition. Autopilot also keeps a per-PRD **decision audit log** at `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/<prd-base>-audit.md`, **rendered once at Phase 9 finalize from the `state.json` decision arrays** (`autonomous_decisions`, `deferred_decisions`, `doubts`). `state.json` is the single in-run source of truth — decisions are NOT mirrored to `audit.md` incrementally per decision. Each rendered entry carries a **source** label (`autonomous`, `deferred`, or `doubt`); cycle/phase context goes in the entry body so the Phase 9 `decisions.md` projection can filter autonomous entries by label. The render is `autopilot render audit` (PRD 00107); the label set and the projection live in `references/audit-log-format.md`.

**Invariant:** every state mutation that advances `phase` SHOULD also set `next_phase` to the same value. The three gates are `build` | `review` | `done` (plus `paused`). `build` is ONE session: selection, catchup, design, planning, and work all run under `phase: "build"` with no mid-build handoff. The review surface runs in its own fresh session; blind and doubt scrutiny are LENSES inside every review cycle (Blake and Bob in `review-work-completion`'s roster), not separate phases — reviewers get isolated contexts by construction (subagent prompts, external CLIs). Legacy `blind`/`doubt` phase values in pre-00015 state files map to `review` on resume. Per-task implementor tiering inside `/autopilot:work` is unchanged. The authoritative resume signal is `phase` + `phases_completed`; build sub-step skipping is by ARTIFACT (capsule freshness, design-doc-exists, tasks-exist, all-done), not by `phases_completed` membership. This resume decision (phase + phases_completed + artifact checks → next step) is encoded canonically in `cli/resume.py` (`scripts/resume_target.py` re-exports it), which `scripts/test_autopilot_resume.py` imports — editing the resume logic there flips a test red rather than silently drifting from this prose. Run `autopilot resume-target` at Phase 0 to print what that encoding says the next action is, and reconcile it against the handler you are about to follow: a disagreement means the prose and the encoded contract have drifted, and the encoding wins. It also runs the schema-version preflight, so an old or future `state.json` is surfaced there rather than resumed blindly. It answers for the `build` and `review` gates; `phase: "done"` returns `unknown phase: done` by design — the done gate is routed by the table above, not by this function.

### Retention

Everything under `docs/dev/project-management/` is tracked work-management state. It is never age-purged. Completed PRDs, reviews, designs, audit logs, reports, ledgers, deferred records, telemetry, and the project capsule therefore remain available to remotes. Runtime control files such as `state.json`, marker files, lane files, and wave slots may still be removed by their explicit lifecycle transitions, but never by a generic stale-file collector.

- **Durable** (never delete): `docs/dev/project-management/prds/done/` and its PRDs, `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/` (per-cycle review files, blind/doubt reviews, and the `<prd-base>-audit.md` audit renders), `docs/dev/project-management/designs/` (per-PRD design docs), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/` (batch reports), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred/` (the `{batch_id}-deferred.json` records), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/loop-metrics.jsonl` (the ledger mirror, the durable copy to read), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/attempts.jsonl` (per-attempt rows appended at every PRD close, `references/state-schema.md` § Attempt ledger), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/custody.jsonl` (the custody journal, the push guard's restore source when the `critical-on-master` marker is removed, `references/state-schema.md` § Custody journal), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (per-dispatch timing rows and session-handoff edges, `work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry), `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md`, and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/<wave id>-wave.md` (the ledger mirror of the wave summary report `autopilot wave assemble` writes, the durable copy to read). The `reports/<wave id>-wave.md` copy it mirrors is tracked as well, but the ledger mirror is the one to read.
- **Not durable** (untracked scratch): `docs/dev/tmp/`, the only tree `purge-devtmp` touches.
- **Disposable** (removed by their lifecycle transitions, by name): `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-session.log`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/wrapper.log`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/paused-by-operator`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` (re-rendered at every handoff), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.session-left` (overwritten at every loop-mode handoff), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/lanes/` (one marker per live CLI reviewer lane, removed when the lane exits), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` (at batch end only — in loop mode the wrapper archives it to `reports/{batch_id}-state-final.json`; see `references/phase-done.md`), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/wave.json`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/wave-slots/` and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/review-paths` (a wave's control file, its per-wave review-slot directory, and the review's path-scoping list — the last removed with the assembly worktree at wave end, same lifecycle as the other two — none is a durable PRD-lifecycle artifact; `references/waves.md`), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/replan-context.md`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json.bak`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/**/*.lock` (the flock files beside `state.json` and beside each `deferred/*.json`), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.turn-counts.json`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.handoff-requested`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.cap-fired`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/park-requested`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-verification.json`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.review-gate-blocks`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.review-gate-failed`, and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.lane-guard-blocks`.

The machine form of this list is `docs/dev/project-management/.gitignore`, shipped by the Phase 0 `mkdir` step; a test keeps the two in step.

Temporary review context and other reproducible scratch material belongs under the globally ignored `docs/dev/tmp/` tree. `purge-devtmp` operates only there, preserves files linked to live PRDs, and never traverses `docs/dev/project-management/`.

Batch end and cleanup steps enumerate lifecycle-owned runtime files explicitly; they never remove a directory wholesale. This keeps a completed PRD's complete review trail intact after the batch closes (`references/design-rationale.md` § Verified moves).

### Resuming

When `/autopilot:run-autopilot` is invoked and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` exists with `batch.completed_prds`, this is a continuation after a session restart. Preserve `batch.completed_prds` (including `batch.id`) and proceed to the build gate's Phase 0 to pick the next PRD.

Delete `state.pause_reason` from `state.json` if present — unconditional, on every invocation, NOT gated on `batch.completed_prds`. A new session means any pause is being resumed; `pause_reason` belongs only to an unresolved pause and is not overwritten by normal progression, so it must be cleared here or it halts the resumed PRD's next hand-off. Cap-pause detection is unaffected — it keys on `cap_pause_reason`, which this delete does not touch.

### Operator runbook (unattended batches)

All interaction with a running `autoclaude` batch happens at session boundaries — the only safe point. (Operator-shell commands for the human's own terminal, not for the model's Bash tool — `tail -f` would hang a session and pipes are hook-blocked.)

- **Watch**: `tail -f docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-session.log` — the wrapper tees the live event log of the running headless turn there.
- **Pause**: `touch docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` — the wrapper consumes the marker at the next session boundary, notifies "paused by operator", and stops the loop with state intact. It leaves `paused-by-operator` behind so tracon shows `⏸ paused` rather than `⚠ orphaned`; plain `autoclaude` resumes (nothing to clear, no decision to make). The marker may carry a JSON reason, `{"reason": "..."}`, which the stop line and the notification quote; a session that stands down for a peer writes one with a `condition` beside it, after asking the peer first (§ Session Loop, stand-down procedure).
- **Take over**: with the loop stopped (pause marker, or Ctrl-C on the wrapper), run `/autopilot:run-autopilot` in a normal interactive session — resume-by-artifact reads the same `state.json`, and full interactive semantics (questions, PAUSEs) apply because `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is unset. Restart `autoclaude` afterwards to go unattended again.
- **Resume after a PAUSE** (`phase: "paused"` in `state.json`, "session paused" banner/ntfy): same take-over recipe, and it is the ONLY way forward — re-running `autoclaude` reads the paused state and exits again immediately. Interactively, the phase that paused re-runs with `AskUserQuestion` available, so the blockers that halted the loop are asked as decisions instead. Answer them, let the session hand off or finish the PRD, then re-run `autoclaude`.
- **Un-park a sidelined PRD**: a PRD the loop parked (a `wrapper_died` death-park, or a loop-mode `design_gate` / `blocking_escalation` stall) sits in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/` with its stall recorded in the batch deferred JSON; the batch kept draining without it. To resume it, `mv docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/<00XXX-…>.md docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog/` (keep the `00XXX-` prefix). Autopilot never reads `hold/`, so the next `/autopilot:run-autopilot` (or `autoclaude` relaunch) re-selects it from `backlog/` and re-enters the build gate, reusing its existing design doc via the Phase 1.5 artifact skip (a `design_gate` park then re-fires the gate interactively). Batch-end review lists every parked PRD (`{m} stalled`), so none is silently forgotten.
- **Forensics**: `claude --resume <session-id>` (the id is in the init event at the top of `last-session.log`) reopens a finished headless conversation for questioning. Harmless by construction: sessions are disposable; `state.json` plus the artifacts are the only orchestration contract, so a resumed chat cannot fork the loop.
- **Run a wave (parallel lanes)**: `autopilot wave plan`, then `autopilot wave launch`, `autopilot wave status` and `autopilot wave abort` — one detached loop per lane worktree, each over its own slice of the backlog. Full operator surface, including what is deferred: `references/waves.md`.
- **Product QA (agoge)**: once a batch drains at least one PRD, the loop runs a single product-QA pass (`/run-agoge` over the repo), logging to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/{batch}-agoge.log`. A batch that drained nothing skips it with a line saying so; a QA failure is recorded and swallowed, never turning a successful drain into a failed one. `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_CAP` (default 3600s) bounds a hung run.

- **One loop per repo**: a second `autoclaude` on a repo that already has a live loop refuses to start, naming the incumbent loop's PID (both the tracon front-end and the plain/headless path check the loop registry via `scripts/tracon_wrapper_alive.py` before registering). This prevents two loops double-draining the backlog and racing `state.json` writes. If the refusal is wrong (the named PID is dead), the stale registry entry is pruned automatically on the next launch; force it by deleting `~/.claude/autopilot-loops/<pid>.json`.

A running headless turn is interrupted by the wrapper's wall-clock cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX`, default 7200s; review-phase launches use `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX_REVIEW`, default 10800s) and, independently, by the idle watchdog at any point after launch: it kills a session whose log has gone silent for `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE` seconds (default 1200s; `0` disables pre-cap idle kill, restoring the old kill-at-cap-only behavior) as long as nothing is in flight (`session_busy`) - this fires before the cap, not only past it. Fifteen minutes before the cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_WARN`, seconds, `0` disables) the wrapper writes the same `.handoff-requested` marker the context-cap hook writes, so a session that reaches a task boundary inside that window hands off cleanly instead of being killed mid-task. Once the wall-clock cap itself is reached, the same idle-silence watchdog applies, or the session is SIGTERMed at twice the cap (the ceiling), whichever comes first.

A PRD whose session metrics ledger spend since `state.prd_budget_since` exceeds `_AUTOPILOT_PRD_BUDGET_USD` (float; default 300; `0` disables; an unparseable value keeps 300) is parked (`park_site: "budget"`) rather than left to burn further sessions unattended.

The agoge run above arms the runtime-security lane by default, passing `--authorized autoclaude-drain`; `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_AUTHORIZED=0` is the kill switch, dropping just that flag so QA still runs, unarmed. Only the literal `0` disables it: anything else, including `false`, `no`, `off`, or `0` with a trailing space, leaves it armed, because a security brake should fail toward armed, not away from it. It brakes a default-on assertion; it is not a separate way to invoke one, since the assertion itself stays invocation-only.

### Task Counts

`tasks_total` and `tasks_completed` are maintained by whoever writes the `state.tasks` snapshot: recompute both in the same write — `tasks_total = len(tasks)`, `tasks_completed = count(status == "completed")` (the pidash-era PostToolUse sync hook is retired, PRD 00063). The model does not re-derive these counts by any other means; the arithmetic runs on the snapshot already in hand. Keep `state.tasks` accurate at phase transitions and recompute the counts alongside each `tasks` snapshot, applying all three with `statectl set` (§ State Management), keeping the dashboard progress bar live.

### Live Dashboard

`autoclaude` launches `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`) in the foreground by default (PRD 00062), so the loop terminal shows the live dashboard with no extra step. It reads `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — no action needed from autopilot beyond keeping the state file updated. `q` detaches (loop keeps running, wrapper prints the reattach command), `p` pauses at the next session boundary, `Ctrl-C` stops the loop with full cleanup. When there is no tty, no `uv`, or `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0`, the loop terminal shows the `render_stream.py` fallback with per-lane subagent tags instead. Full operator surface: `references/dashboard-format.md`.
