# Bundled default sysup configuration.
#
# Reproduces the behaviour of the former `sysup mac` and `sysup wsl`
# subcommands, host-selected via each entry's `when`. It is the lowest-priority
# layer: any `buvis-sysup.yaml` (or its machine-local `.local.yaml` twin) in the
# config stack deep-merges on top by key, so a machine can add, reorder, or
# disable (`enabled: false`) an entry without redefining this base.

commands:
  # --- macOS (former `sysup mac`) -----------------------------------------
  brew:
    order: 10
    when: { os: darwin, check: brew }
    sudo: true
    # Homebrew resets the sudo ticket before its first sudo call, so a cask
    # upgrade prompts for a password; captured mode hid that prompt. A TTY also
    # turns on brew's "proceed with the upgrade?" prompt, hence --no-ask.
    interactive: true
    steps:
      - brew update
      # Casks that update themselves (browsers, editors) are left to their own
      # updater instead of being reinstalled on every run.
      - HOMEBREW_NO_UPGRADE_AUTO_UPDATES_CASKS=1 brew upgrade --quiet --no-ask
      - brew cleanup

  npm-check:
    order: 20
    when: { os: darwin, check: npm-check }
    interactive: true
    steps:
      - npm-check -gu

  python-packages:
    order: 30
    when: { os: darwin }
    use: pip-outdated

  # Pin freestanding uv tools to the global python minor before uv tool upgrade.
  uv-tool-python:
    order: 35
    when: { os: darwin, check: uv }
    use: uv-tool-python

  uv:
    order: 40
    when: { os: darwin, check: uv }
    steps:
      - uv python upgrade
      - uv tool upgrade --all

  helm:
    order: 50
    when: { os: darwin, check: helm }
    use: helm-repo-update

  # Before mise: mise's `cargo:` tools are built with the toolchain this updates.
  rustup:
    order: 55
    when: { os: darwin, check: rustup }
    steps:
      - rustup update

  # `mise upgrade` deletes replaced tool-version dirs that the inherited PATH
  # still points at, so it must run after every other tool lookup — hence the
  # highest `order` among the macOS entries.
  mise:
    order: 60
    when: { os: darwin, check: mise }
    steps:
      - mise self-update --yes
      - mise upgrade

  # Moves mise pipx tools pinned with `--managed-python --python X.Y` onto the
  # global mise python minor. After `mise upgrade` so it sees the new global
  # python; before nvim so pynvim is settled when Mason spawns nvim.
  pipx-python:
    order: 65
    when: { os: darwin, check: mise }
    use: pipx-python

  # --- Cross-platform (former standalone `sysup nvim`) --------------------
  # The old `sysup nvim` subcommand had no platform guard — it ran wherever
  # nvim resolved. `order: 70` keeps it after `mise upgrade` (and after every
  # macOS tool lookup), so a version-manager churn that replaces the nvim
  # binary happens before the headless Mason update spawns it.
  nvim:
    order: 70
    when: { check: nvim }
    use: nvim-mason

  # --- WSL / Linux (former `sysup wsl`) -----------------------------------
  apt:
    order: 10
    when: { os: linux, check: apt }
    steps:
      - sudo apt update
      - sudo apt upgrade -y
      - sudo apt autoremove -y

  snap:
    order: 20
    when: { os: linux, check: snap }
    steps:
      - sudo snap refresh

# Session-level capabilities that run before any command. sudo priming caches
# credentials up front for steps that invoke sudo; Homebrew resets the ticket itself.
prime:
  - sudo-prime

# Expiring credentials checked before every ordinary run (PRD 00096). gh-agent
# is a disabled template: in buvis-sysup.local.yaml set `with.probe` to a
# `gh api` path that needs private-repository access (for example
# repos/<owner>/<private-repo>) and `enabled: true`. The other fields merge in.
expiry:
  gh-agent:
    enabled: false
    use: gh-token-expiry
    with:
      config_dir: ~/.config/gh-agent
    warn_days: 30
    refresh:
      instructions: |
        1. Open https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new
        2. Token name: gh-agent. Resource owner: buvis. Expiration: 1 year.
        3. Repository access: All repositories.
        4. Permissions: Pull requests (read and write), Issues (read and write),
           Actions (read), Commit statuses (read), Contents (read), Metadata (read).
        5. Generate the token, copy it, and paste it at the prompt below.
      commands:
        - argv: gh auth login --hostname github.com --with-token --insecure-storage
          env: { GH_CONFIG_DIR: ~/.config/gh-agent }
          stdin: secret

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.17.0] - 2026-11-04

### Added

- **sysup**: on macOS, `rustup update` runs before `mise upgrade` when `rustup` is installed, so the Rust toolchain stays current and mise's `cargo:` tools build with it.
- **gems**: wheels for Python 3.15 (macOS arm64, Linux x64 and arm64, Windows x64), so installing on 3.15 no longer needs a Rust toolchain; `pyyaml` and `xattr` publish no 3.15 wheels yet, so pip and uv build them from source on 3.15 (a C compiler is needed for `xattr`).
- **backup**: TTY runs show per-instance live progress and elapsed time, with input-byte percentages capped at 99% for Python archives and activity only for system tar; `--quiet` hides live status while preserving final results and summary counts.
- **backup**: `--jobs` controls concurrent archive instances (default three); cancellation stops new work, joins workers, stops tar and cleans temporary files while preserving completed results and backups; interruption exits with status 130.
- **backup**: `--plan` previews metadata-only run/skip/fail decisions, reasons and existing-output replacement markers; selected outputs share one timestamp and colliding paths are rejected before plan, run or dry-run execution. Missing inputs report the same errors as a run; a metadata error fails only its instance, keeping its expanded source, while preserving collision checks.
- **backup**: optional `items` bundle literal source-relative files and directories into one archive, preserving empty directories and symlinks while applying inherited exclusions and `.bkpignore` rules.
- **backup**: per-instance `inherit_excludes`, `exclude_remove` and `exclude_add` control inherited exclusions for archives and `--show-excludes`, which still lists the resolved patterns sorted.

### Changed

- **backup**: missing sources and bundles with no surviving members now warn and skip without touching previous archives; each run reports archived or previewed, skipped, and failed step counts. Existing non-directory sources, unreadable sources and unreadable selected items still fail instead of counting as missing; a skipped bundle names its source.

### Fixed

- **backup**: a bundle's `out` may now lie under `source` when it is outside every selected item (for example `~/.local/backup/settings.tar.gz` for `items: [.gitconfig, .npmrc]`); an `out` equal to or inside a selected item still fails in run, `--dry-run` and `--plan`.
- **backup**: progress returns to archiving when a failure after system tar finishes triggers the Python fallback.
- **backup**: interruption during submission or result collection preserves every instance's outcome and finishes cleanup without waiting for a lost completion notification.
- **sysup**: a `timeout` on a captured multi-command shell step now stops the whole step; before, only bash died and the command it was waiting on kept running. Such a step runs in its own process group, so Ctrl-C is forwarded to it, a terminal prompt it raises stops it until the timeout, and a command it runs as root through `sudo` is still out of reach and survives. Interactive steps and steps without a timeout are unchanged

## [0.16.0] - 2026-10-29

### Added

- **sysup**: a step in a run entry, and a refresh command, may be written as a plain shell line such as `HOMEBREW_NO_UPGRADE_AUTO_UPDATES_CASKS=1 brew upgrade --quiet`, run by `bash -eo pipefail -c`, so variables, pipes, `&&` and `VAR=1 cmd` prefixes work as typed and a failing command anywhere in a pipe fails the step; an argv array still runs without a shell, and either may be an `{argv, env}` object whose `env` is merged over the parent environment for that step only (`~` expanded). An empty step is rejected when the config loads instead of failing mid-run

### Changed

- **sysup**: the bundled entries are written as shell lines; `brew` upgrades with `HOMEBREW_NO_UPGRADE_AUTO_UPDATES_CASKS=1` and `--quiet`, leaving self-updating casks to their own updater; sudo priming triggers on any step that invokes `sudo`, not only one whose argv starts with it

## [0.15.3] - 2026-10-28
